fields.Name: ORD-27 - Advance Order State
fields.Description: Orders.AdvanceOrderState (ADV1-ADV11) - moving an already-booked order up the status ladder for back-office entry of something that has ALREADY happened: a counter sale, a shipment that went out before anyone opened the system, a migration. Composing and booking an order is order.Save() through the entity graph and is covered by order-booking; what is left here is the part a save cannot do. The check that carries the bundle is ADV8. The tempting implementation is a single UPDATE setting Status='Fulfilled'; it is faster, it passes any assertion that reads the order's own fields, and applied to an order that never confirmed it produces something that looks complete with no ledger behind it - the failure nothing downstream can detect, because the order reconciles perfectly against itself and the revenue simply never existed. ADV8 asserts the operation refuses to touch such an order at all.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: A Confirmed order reaches Posted and books exactly once, so advancing past the lock does not count revenue twice; the ledger survives the climb, with balanced entries that really exist and an entry count read back rather than assumed; reaching Fulfilled marks the fulfillable LINES and not merely the header, so the queue cannot keep offering work the order claims to have done; an order whose product type requires no fulfilment reaches Fulfilled anyway rather than stranding every service and subscription sale; the transition trail records each rung so a bulk import shows where an order stopped; Draft, Quoted and Confirmed are refused because those are reached by saving the order, and Voided is refused because voiding is a separate decision; an order that never booked is refused outright and is neither moved nor given an invented ledger; a stated reason is recorded on the order that skipped the usual path; advancing to Fulfilled writes no additional journal entry; and re-advancing an order that is already there succeeds without booking again, so a resumed migration is not mistaken for a broken one.
